newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco oil firms to invest $543.5 mln by end 2001.
newsitem.headline: Morocco oil firms to invest $543.5 mln by end 2001.

text.p: Morocco's oil firms plan to invest 5.0 billion dirhams (US$543.5 million) under a five-year plan aims to upgrade the sector and ensure a 60-day security stock, an official at the energy ministry said.
The decision was taken during a meeting between representatives of Morocco's 10 oil firms and government officials, presided by Prime Minister Abdellatif Filali on Thursday, the official said.
He said the meeting examined and agreed on three main issues:
-- A five-year plan under which the firms will invest 5.0 billion dirhams to upgrade the installations of fuel and gas products.
-- To reconstitute a security stock of fuel aimed at reaching by end September 1997 more than 3.2 billion dirhams.
-- Necessity of ensuring the profitability of oil firms to permit the needed investments for the domestic market's fuel and gas supply within the respect of security and environment rules.
The meeting also urged the international compagnies to intensify their research and prospecting activities for oil in the country, he added.
Morocco, which gradually liberalized oil imports in 1995, plans to privatize its oil refineries Samir and Societe Cherifienne des Petroles in the first half of 1997, officials said.
With capacity of more than 5.0 million tonnes of crude, Samir is Morocco's main oil refinery, accounting for about 80 percent of all crude imports.
Seven distribution networks for petroleum products were privatized in 1993 and 1994, and state holdings were bought by foreign firms including, Royal Dutch/Shell and Total SA.
Morocco, which has no oil of its own, imports all its energy mainly from the Gulf countries, including Iran.
According to provisional figures received by Reuters, Morocco imported 5.89 million tonnes of crude oil in 1996, a drop of 14 percent from 6.75 million tonnes in 1995.
"We expect crude imports to stagnate at around 6.0 million tonnes in 1997 due to a decline of fuel consumption for the second consecutive year," said an expert at Energy Ministry.
State-owned electricity utility Office National d'Electricite (ONE) changing style of management and rational energy policy was behind this decline, the expert said.
"ONE's increasing consumption of coal instead of fuel was also a factor for the decreasing crude imports," he said.
Morocco imported around 3.0 million tonnes of coal in 1996 against 2.0 million tonnes in 1995, the expert added.
According to government officials, a total liberalization of the energy sector is expected by the end of 2002.

Based in Morocco's financial center of Casablanca, the oil firms achieve an estimated 20 billion dirhams turnover per year and employ a staff of 20,000. The group has 1,800 filling stations including in the disputed Western Sahara.
($1= 9.2 dirhams)
